title: Trump Wants an 'AI Force' — and Says AI Fears Are a 'Hoax'
summary: Imagine a computer program so smart it could change the whole world. That's called artificial intelligence, or AI. On Saturday, President Donald Trump posted on social media that he will create an 'AI Force' and pick an 'AI tsar' — a leader in charge of AI. He said his team 'will not in any way hinder or stifle the growth' of AI. That means he doesn't want to slow it down. Trump said AI 'is the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger and more impactful, possibly as much as 25% of our Country's GDP.' GDP is the total money a country makes. He also wants the U.S. to stay ahead of China in AI. The two countries are rivals in tech, and AI will come up when Trump meets China's President Xi Jinping next week. Trump says fears about AI dangers are a 'hoax' — meaning he thinks they're not real. But some big AI companies disagree. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google make chatbots called Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini. They have shared times when their chatbots were used for bad things. Anthropic's boss, Dario Amodei, asked the industry to slow down and follow rules. Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk of xAI said they agree. In the UK, a group of lawmakers says new AI laws are needed to protect people's rights.
why_it_matters: AI chatbots are already part of homework, games and apps, so the rules leaders make now will shape how safe and fair that technology is for you.

background_read: Artificial intelligence, or AI (computer programs that can learn and answer questions), is being built by companies like Anthropic (which makes the chatbot Claude) and OpenAI (which makes ChatGPT).
The Industrial Revolution (a time when machines changed how people worked and lived) started long ago, in the 1700s.
Countries like the United States and China (whose president is Xi Jinping) are racing to lead in new technology, so their leaders often talk about it together.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump, who posted on social media about creating an 'AI Force' and picking an 'AI tsar'.
WHAT: He said he will not slow AI down and called fears about AI dangers a 'hoax'.
WHERE: The United States, which he wants to keep ahead of China; AI will also come up when he meets China's President Xi Jinping next week.
WHY: Trump thinks AI could be the next big revolution and as much as 25% of the country's GDP, while big AI companies and UK lawmakers say rules are needed.

perspectives.description: Trump and his team say AI could bring huge new wealth and jobs, so the country should rush ahead without slowing the technology down, especially to stay ahead of China.

Companies like Anthropic, OpenAI and Google warn that their chatbots have been used for bad things, and their leaders — Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk — asked the industry to slow down and follow rules.
In the UK, a group of lawmakers says new AI laws are needed to protect people's rights, because companies alone may not keep people safe.
